data.body:
rebar-debug FINAL REPORT — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1402.

PROBLEM. A stalled Cloud pagination cursor produced a silently degraded snapshot instead of
aborting the pass.

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE. `RunawayPaginationError` was declared `class RunawayPaginationError(RuntimeError)`
(acli_graph.py:29), so it sat outside `BackendPaginationStallError`'s hierarchy. `fetch_snapshot`'s
three enrichment re-raise clauses match on that CORE type (fetcher.py:621 parent, :668 comment,
:708 issuelink), so all three MISSED Cloud's error and the broad `except Exception` fail-open
beneath each (:625/:672/:712) swallowed it.

PROOF. Runtime, not static. Drove the real `fetch_snapshot` (loaded from source, `_load_acli`
patched) with a stub whose `get_parent_map` raises `RunawayPaginationError`:
  WARNING fetcher: parent enrichment failed (RunawayPaginationError(...)); snapshot written
  without parent data (degraded)  ->  SWALLOWED, snapshot written, pass returned.
This discriminates against the rival hypothesis that the transport re-raises (acli_graph.py:304/
394/477) are incomplete: those fire correctly — the loss is one layer up, and it is a type-hierarchy
miss, not a missing handler.

TEST (RED -> GREEN, held out). tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py,
+179 lines:
  * `test_a_cloud_cursor_stall_escapes_every_fetch_snapshot_enrichment_fail_open[parent|comment|
    issuelinks]` — a token-repeating Cloud REST stub driven through the REAL `fetch_snapshot`, with
    the REAL reader raising from the REAL shared `_iter_cursor_pages` walk (never an injected
    exception, which would prove only that `raise` re-raises). Keys on the requested `fields` so
    exactly one enrichment stalls per case and each handler is reached in turn.
  * `test_the_cloud_stall_error_is_the_core_stall_type` — the mechanism stated directly, plus
    `RuntimeError` must stay in the MRO.
  * `test_an_ordinary_enrichment_failure_still_fails_open_and_writes_the_snapshot[x3]` — negative
    control.
Verified RED first for the right reason (3x "DID NOT RAISE" with the swallow visible in the
captured log, plus the MRO assertion). The oracle was moved OUT of the tree before the fix subagent
ran, which was told the test path was off-limits and given only the root cause + contract. After
the fix: 49/49 green. MUTATION CHECK: restoring the `RuntimeError` base returned exactly those 4
tests to RED, then the fix was restored.

FIX. acli_graph.py, +13/-1: `class RunawayPaginationError(BackendPaginationStallError)`, the core
import, and a docstring paragraph recording why that base. fetcher.py untouched.

SCOPE & SAFETY.
  * Caller sweep clear: `except RunawayPaginationError` sites unaffected (same class);
    `except RuntimeError` sites unaffected (`BackendPaginationStallError` subclasses `RuntimeError`,
    so it stays in the MRO); jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:96 is DC-only and cannot see this error.
  * Restoration, not creation — no new entry point, command, or user-visible artifact.
  * No new dependency; the adapter->core import direction already exists (jira_datacenter/_base.py:19).
  * No test weakened: the 179 lines are purely additive, no pre-existing test body edited.
  * Regression: 2271 passed in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/; `make lint` and `make typecheck` green.

SIBLINGS (Step 7, both axes).
  * Construct sweep — the class is "an adapter-local pagination-stall error outside the core
    hierarchy". Only three types exist in this family repo-wide: `BackendPaginationStallError`
    (core), `RunawayPaginationError` (this fix), and `SilentTruncationError` (fetcher.py:108).
    One hit, fixed.
  * Parity census — rule: "a pagination stall raised by any adapter must be nameable by core's
    re-raise clauses." Cloud `adapters/jira` = was MISSING, fixed. DC `adapters/jira_datacenter`
    = holds (_base.py:187 raises the core type directly). `adapters/jira_family` = N/A, no pager.
    fetcher's own base-scan pager `_iter_pages` = N/A: its `SilentTruncationError` is raised from
    call sites at fetcher.py:397/:554, both ABOVE the enrichment try blocks, so no fail-open can
    absorb it (and fetcher.py:511 documents it as propagating). Dual-direction (outbound writes)
    = N/A, no whole-project paged read. No MISSING slot left undisposed.

RESIDUAL RISK. None observed beyond the fixed defect. The structural guard against recurrence is
the new `test_the_cloud_stall_error_is_the_core_stall_type` assertion: any future stall error that
drifts out of the core hierarchy fails it.

REPLICATION. The original report's scenario no longer reproduces — the same probe that printed
">>> SWALLOWED: snapshot written" now prints ">>> PROPAGATED".
